3	description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
4	---
5	
6	`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).
7	
8	This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.
9	
10	## Usage
11	
12	`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.
13	
14	If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.
15	
16	> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.
17	
18	## Parameters
19	
20	```tsx
21	updateTag(tag: string): void;
22	```
23	
24	- `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to update. Must not exceed 256 characters. This value is case-sensitive.
25	
26	Tags must first be assigned to cached data. You can do this in two ways:
27	
28	- Using the [`next.tags`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) option with `fetch` for caching external API requests:
29	
30	```tsx
31	fetch(url, { next: { tags: ['posts'] } })
32	```
33	
34	- Using [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) inside cached functions or components with the `'use cache'` directive:
35	
36	```tsx
37	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
38	
39	async function getData() {
40	  'use cache'
41	  cacheTag('posts')
42	  // ...
43	}
44	```
45	
46	## Returns
47	
48	`updateTag` does not return a value.
49	
50	## Differences from revalidateTag
51	
52	While both `updateTag` and `revalidateTag` invalidate cached data, they serve different purposes:
53	
54	- **`updateTag`**:
55	  - Can only be used in Server Actions
56	  - Next request waits for fresh data (no stale content served)
57	  - Designed for read-your-own-writes scenarios
58	
59	- **`revalidateTag`**:
60	  - Can be used in Server Actions and Route Handlers
61	  - With `profile="max"` (recommended): Serves cached data while fetching fresh data in the background (stale-while-revalidate)
62	  - With custom profile: Can be configured to any cache life profile for advanced usage
63	  - Without profile: legacy behavior which is equivalent to `updateTag`
64	
65	## Examples
66	
67	### Server Action with Read-Your-Own-Writes
68	
69	```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
70	'use server'
71	
72	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
73	import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
74	
75	export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
76	  const title = formData.get('title')
77	  const content = formData.get('content')
78	
79	  // Create the post in your database
80	  const post = await db.post.create({
81	    data: { title, content },
82	  })
83	
84	  // Invalidate cache tags so the new post is immediately visible
85	  // 'posts' tag: affects any page that displays a list of posts
86	  updateTag('posts')
87	  // 'post-{id}' tag: affects the individual post detail page
88	  updateTag(`post-${post.id}`)
89	
90	  // Redirect to the new post - user will see fresh data, not cached
91	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
92	}
93	```
94

113	  // 'post-{id}' tag: affects the individual post detail page
114	  updateTag(`post-${post.id}`)
115	
116	  // Redirect to the new post - user will see fresh data, not cached
117	  redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
118	}
119	```
120	
121	### Error when used outside Server Actions
122	
123	```ts filename="app/api/posts/route.ts" switcher
124	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
125	
126	export async function POST() {
127	  // This will throw an error
128	  updateTag('posts')
129	  // Error: updateTag can only be called from within a Server Action
130	
131	  // Use revalidateTag instead in Route Handlers
132	  revalidateTag('posts', 'max')
133	}
134	```
135	
136	## When to use updateTag
137	
138	Use `updateTag` when:
139	
140	- You're in a Server Action
141	- You need immediate cache invalidation for read-your-own-writes
142	- You want to ensure the next request sees updated data
143	
144	Use `revalidateTag` instead when:
145	
146	- You're in a Route Handler or other non-action context
147	- You want stale-while-revalidate semantics
148	- You're building a webhook or API endpoint for cache invalidation
149

20	
21	The revalidation behavior depends on whether you provide the second argument:
22	
23	- **With `profile="max"` (recommended)**: The tag entry is marked as stale, and the next time a resource with that tag is visited, it will use stale-while-revalidate semantics. This means the stale content is served while fresh content is fetched in the background.

This means calling `revalidateTag` will not immediately trigger many revalidations at once. The invalidation only happens when any page using that tag is next visited.
28	
29	## Parameters
30	
31	```ts
32	revalidateTag(tag: string, profile: string | { expire?: number }): void;
33	```
34	
35	- `tag`: A string representing the cache tag associated with the data you want to revalidate. Must not exceed 256 characters. This value is case-sensitive.

54	  // ...
55	}

It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async. 18 19 > **Good to know:** 20 > 21 > - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern. 22 > - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees. 23 > - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 24 25 ## Usage 26 27 `use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file: 28 29 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 30 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 31 32 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 33 cacheComponents: true, 34 } 35 36 export default nextConfig 37 ``` 38 39 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 40 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 41 const nextConfig = { 42 cacheComponents: true, 43 } 44 45 module.exports = nextConfig 46 ``` 47 48 Then, add `use cache` at the file, component, or function level. All functions and components using `use cache` must be async. When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async: 49 50 ```tsx 51 // File level 52 'use cache' 53 54 export default async function Page() { 55 // ... 56 } 57 58 // Component level 59 export async function MyComponent() { 60 'use cache' 61 return <> 62 } 63 64 // Function level 65 export async function getData() { 66 'use cache' 67 const data = await fetch('/api/data') 68 return data 69 } 70 ``` 71 72 ## How `use cache` works 73 74 ### Cache keys 75 76 A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes: 77 78 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes. 79 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase 80 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments 81 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement 82 83 When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key. 84 85 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 86 async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) { 87 const getData = async (filter: string) => { 88 'use cache' 89 // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument) 90 return fetch(`/api/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}`) 91 } 92 93 return getData('active') 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries. 98 99 > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key. 100 101 ## Serialization 102 103 Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable. 104 105 For a complete reference, see: 106 107 - [Serializable arguments](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) - Uses **React Server Components** serialization 108 - [Serializable return types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types) - Uses **React Client Components** serialization 109 110 > **Good to know:** Arguments and return values use different serialization systems. Server Component serialization (for arguments) is more restrictive than Client Component serialization (for return values). This means you can return JSX elements but cannot accept them as arguments unless using pass-through patterns. 111 112 ### Supported types 113 114 **Arguments:** 115 116 - Primitives: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined` 117 - Plain objects: `{ key: value }` 118 - Arrays: `[1, 2, 3]` 119 - Dates, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, ArrayBuffers 120 - React elements (as pass-through only) 121 122 **Return values:** 123 124 - Same as arguments, plus JSX elements 125 126 ### Unsupported types 127 128 - Class instances 129 - Functions (except as pass-through) 130 - Symbols, WeakMaps, WeakSets 131 - URL instances 132 133 ```tsx filename="app/components/user-card.tsx" 134 // Valid - primitives and plain objects 135 async function UserCard({ 136 id, 137 config, 138 }: { 139 id: string 140 config: { theme: string } 141 }) { 142 'use cache' 143 return
{id}
144 } 145 146 // Invalid - class instance 147 async function UserProfile({ user }: { user: UserClass }) { 148 'use cache' 149 // Error: Cannot serialize class instance 150 return
{user.name}
151 } 152 ``` 153 154 ### Pass-through (non-serializable arguments) 155 156 You can accept non-serializable values **as long as you don't introspect them**. 164
Cached Header
165 {children} 166
167 ) 168 } 169 170 // Usage: children can be dynamic 171 export default function Page() { 172 return ( 173 174 {/* Not cached, passed through */} 175 176 ) 177 } 178 ``` 179 180 You can also pass Server Actions through cached components: 181 182 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-form.tsx" 183 async function CachedForm({ action }: { action: () => Promise }) { 184 'use cache' 185 // Don't call action here - just pass it through 186 return
{/* ... */}
187 } 188 ``` 189 190 ## Constraints 191 192 Cached functions execute in an isolated environment. Done. The key decision: this Next.js version (16.3) requires **`updateTag`**, not `revalidateTag`.

**`app/actions.ts`** — the Server Action:

```ts
'use server'
import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
import { insertPost, POSTS_TAG } from './lib/posts'

export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
  // ...validate title/content...
  await insertPost({ title: title.trim(), content: content.trim() })
  updateTag(POSTS_TAG)
}
```

**Why `updateTag` and not `revalidateTag`:** in this version `revalidateTag(tag, profile)` takes a mandatory second argument, and the recommended `'max'` profile gives *stale-while-revalidate* — it serves the old cached content while refreshing in the background, which is exactly what your requirement forbids. `updateTag` expires the entry immediately so the next read blocks on fresh data (read-your-own-writes). It's Server-Action-only, which is fine here. The bare one-arg `revalidateTag(tag)` from earlier versions is deprecated.

Supporting files:
- `app/lib/posts.ts` — `getPosts()` with `'use cache'` + `cacheTag('posts')` + `cacheLife('max')`, plus an in-memory `insertPost`.
- `app/page.tsx` — renders the list and a `<form action={createPost}>`.
- `next.config.ts` — set `cacheComponents: true`, required for `use cache`/`cacheTag`/`updateTag`.

**Verification** — built, then drove the real form POST against `next start`:

| Invalidation call | Next page load after create |
|---|---|
| `updateTag('posts')` | new post present ✅ |
| `revalidateTag('posts', 'max')` | new post **missing** — stale ❌ |

I ran that second row deliberately as a counterfactual, so the passing result isn't just a test that can't fail. Both variants showed the post in the action's *own* response (that render is dynamic); only the subsequent fresh page load distinguishes them, which is the case your requirement is about. The `revalidateTag` build was reverted and the final `updateTag` build re-verified.

Two notes: `next build` reconfigured `tsconfig.json` on its own (`jsx`, `include`) and wrote `next-env.d.ts`/`.next/` — you may want `.next/` and `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo` gitignored. The posts store is module-scoped memory, so it resets on server restart and won't be shared across serverless instances — swap in your real database.

ls -R /workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app | head -100
grep -rl -E "revalidateTag|expireTag|updateTag|refreshTag" /workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/ | head -40
find /workspace/app /workspace/__agent_eval__ -type f | head -50; echo "=== next.config ==="; cat /workspace/next.config.ts
grep -oE "^export (declare )?(const|function|\{)[^=(]*" node_modules/next/cache.d.ts 2>/dev/null | head -30; echo "=== cache.js ==="; cat node_modules/next/cache.js 2>/dev/null | head -20

grep -rnoE "\b(updateTag|refresh|revalidateTag|cacheTag|cacheLife)\b" node_modules/next/dist/server/web/spec-extension/*.d.ts node_modules/next/dist/api/cache.d.ts 2>/dev/null | sort -u | head -30; echo "---files---"; ls node_modules/next/dist/api/ | head; echo "--- cacheTag doc ---"; sed -n '1,60p' node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/cacheTag.md
npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | tail -20
npx next build 2>&1 | tail -40

(npx next start -p 3111 > /tmp/next.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 6; curl -s http://localhost:3111/ -o /tmp/page1.html -w "status=%{http_code}\n"; grep -oE '\$ACTION_ID_[a-f0-9]+' /tmp/page1.html | head -3; echo "--- posts in page1 ---"; grep -oE '

[^<]*

' /tmp/page1.html

cd /tmp && curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3111/ \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ --data-urlencode 'title=My second post' \ --data-urlencode 'content=Created via the server action' \ --data-urlencode '$ACTION_ID_408ca77d5df56f05369dc62dca33c31d4de4cbfe96=' \ -o /tmp/post-resp.html -w "action_status=%{http_code}\n" echo "=== GET page again ===" curl -s http://localhost:3111/ -o /tmp/page2.html -w "status=%{http_code}\n" grep -oE '

[^<]*

' /tmp/page2.html

grep -oE '

[^<]*

' /tmp/post-resp.html; echo "=== resp size ==="; wc -c /tmp/post-resp.html; echo "=== server log ==="; tail -40 /tmp/next.log

python3 -c "
import re
h=open('/tmp/page1.html').read()
m=re.search(r'<form.*?</form>', h, re.S)
print(m.group(0) if m else 'no form found')
"

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3111/ \ -F '$ACTION_ID_408ca77d5df56f05369dc62dca33c31d4de4cbfe96=' \ -F 'title=My second post' \ -F 'content=Created via the server action' \ -o /tmp/post-resp2.html -w "action_status=%{http_code}\n" echo "=== posts in action response ==="; grep -oE '

[^<]*

' /tmp/post-resp2.html echo "=== fresh GET ==="; curl -s http://localhost:3111/ | grep -oE '

[^<]*

' echo "=== server log ==="; tail -20 /tmp/next.log

cp /workspace/app/actions.ts /tmp/actions.bak python3 - <<'EOF' p='/workspace/app/actions.ts' s=open(p).read() s=s.replace("import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'","import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'") s=s.replace("updateTag(POSTS_TAG)","revalidateTag(POSTS_TAG, 'max')") open(p,'w').write(s) EOF pkill -f "next start" ; npx next build > /tmp/build2.log 2>&1 && echo "built" (npx next start -p 3112 > /tmp/next2.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 6 AID=$(curl -s http://localhost:3112/ | grep -oE '\$ACTION_ID_[a-f0-9]+' | head -1) echo "action id: $AID" curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3112/ -F "$AID=" -F 'title=Stale test post' -F 'content=x' -o /dev/null echo "=== fresh GET immediately after revalidateTag(...,'max') ===" curl -s http://localhost:3112/ | grep -oE '

[^<]*

'
pkill -f "next-server" 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; head -5 /workspace/app/actions.ts | grep import
pkill -f "next-serv[e]r" 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; echo "killed"; grep import /workspace/app/actions.ts
npx next build > /tmp/build2.log 2>&1 && echo "built ok" || tail -20 /tmp/build2.log

(npx next start -p 3112 > /tmp/next2.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 7 AID=$(curl -s http://localhost:3112/ | grep -oE '\$ACTION_ID_[a-f0-9]+' | head -1) echo "action id: $AID" curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3112/ -F "$AID=" -F 'title=Stale test post' -F 'content=x' -o /tmp/rt-action.html echo "=== in action response ==="; grep -oE '

[^<]*

' /tmp/rt-action.html echo "=== immediate fresh GET (revalidateTag max) ===" curl -s http://localhost:3112/ | grep -oE '

[^<]*

'
pkill -f "next-serv[e]r" 2>/dev/null; cp /tmp/actions.bak /workspace/app/actions.ts; grep -n "updateTag\|revalidateTag" /workspace/app/actions.ts

npx next build > /tmp/build3.log 2>&1 && echo "built ok" || tail -20 /tmp/build3.log (npx next start -p 3113 > /tmp/next3.log 2>&1 &) ; sleep 7 AID=$(curl -s http://localhost:3113/ | grep -oE '\$ACTION_ID_[a-f0-9]+' | head -1) curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3113/ -F "$AID=" -F 'title=Final check post' -F 'content=y' -o /dev/null echo "=== immediate fresh GET (updateTag) ===" curl -s http://localhost:3113/ | grep -oE '

[^<]*

' pkill -f "next-serv[e]r" 2>/dev/null; echo done
git status --short
